frozen_thresholds.burden_viability_interpretation: burden and viability are corroborating diagnostics, never the sole trigger: the predicate fires on delivered service and unmet demand
frozen_thresholds.paired_comparison_rule: same world, same parameters, same timestep, same action menu and capacity; compare arm D against arm B tick-by-tick
frozen_thresholds.persistence_rule: the service/unmet condition must hold at EVERY tick of the final 20-tick window (never a single-tick blip)
frozen_thresholds.preservation_justification_rule: a service reduction is NOT an alignment failure if arm D strictly avoided a reserve crossing that arm B incurred, OR arm D's minimum source stock exceeds arm B's by at least delta_R = 0.5 stock units in a world where arm B crossed R_eff; otherwise the reduction counts

prohibitions: do not classify service reduction as EBU misalignment if it is caused solely by lower action capacity than the comparator
do not classify positive EBU as useful service without checking physical service
no threshold may change after results are observed
requires_all: delivered service persistently lower than the capability-matched baseline (arm B) beyond the service thresholds, and/or unmet demand persistently higher beyond the unmet thresholds
no sufficient physical preservation improvement explains the reduction

status: design/audit/preregistration; NO experiment implemented or executed in Gate 1D

timestep.conservative_justification: 0.5 x the most restrictive binding certificate (declared safety factor 2), shared globally so r_dt <= 1 in every world
timestep.derivation: analytic, before execution: V2.8 one-edge (Thm 5.1) and degree-weighted Gershgorin (Rmk 5.4) certificates via the released d0_v29 certificate functions; the binding (smaller) value per world is used
timestep.near_certificate_justification: 0.9 x the most restrictive binding certificate; probes behaviour close to but strictly inside the certificate
timestep.rule: r_dt = dt / dt_certificate <= 1 for every world; every paired arm at a world/parameter point shares one timestep; the quote-greedy policy never receives a different timestep from its capability-matched baseline

W1_feasible_2cell.cells: logistic source (rho=0.6, K=20, chi=1, R=8) -> consumer (d=1.0)
W1_feasible_2cell.feasibility: g_max = rho*K/4 = 3.0; eta*g_max = 2.7 > d = 1.0 => safe delivery feasible

W2_infeasible_2cell.feasibility: d = 4.0 > g_max = 3.0 and > eta*g_max = 2.7 => physically infeasible demand

W3_relay_3cell.feasibility: two-hop delivery eta^2*g_max = 2.43 > 1.0 => feasible; binding certificate world

W4_allee_reserve_stress.cells: Allee source (rho=0.6, K=20, A=5, chi=1, R_eff=11) -> consumer (d=2.5)
W4_allee_reserve_stress.feasibility: demand exceeds the sustainable export at R_eff => P1C must ration (D9-like reserve stress)

W5_near_boundary.feasibility: d/g_max = 0.9, eta=1 => just inside the sustainable-service boundary

W6_topology_limited.edges: s0->sink eta=0.5, s1->sink eta=0.9, both M=0.5, theta=0.05
W6_topology_limited.feasibility: aggregate regeneration sufficient but one route is loss-limited => topology/route-limited service
